questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial to me that the university would have a lot of social opportunities. And the University of Queensland (UQ) has a broad variety of student clubs, so I think that anyone would be able to find at least one, they would like to join. Besides that, it was very important to me that I was able to find courses that I found interesting.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found that the courses were much easier compared to studying at the University of Copenhagen. At times I felt a bit disappointed by this, but it really allowed me to go on trips and explore the country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: UQ has a orientation (O-)week, which provides a lot of information and opportunities to meet other exchange students. They had so many events, that it felt like you had to prioritize between them. However, I chose a 3-weeks course which took place before O-week. Therefore, I had to figure out things before, but UQ has a Student Central where you can go with all your questions, which made it very easy to obtain information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had the e-mail address for the one, who was responsible for UQ's exchange students, so I could also directly ask her. But besides that I really found that the Student Central was very useful during my entire stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through a recommendation from a girl from DTU, who had been on exchange at UQ the year before. That very easy. Moreover, there are a lot of student housing opportunities in Brisbane, so it's fairly easy to choose one of them. However, this is a very expensive solution.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: All the on-campus accommodations are usually for Australians, who just started universities. Living off-campus provides the opportunity to live with students who are a bit older. I lived with other exchange students, but I would recommend finding a shared house through flatmates or something similar. Before you chose your off-campus accommodation, you should look into how easy it is to go to campus. Public transportation is not always the easiest in Brisbane.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's usually very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got the deadline from UCPH very late, so I found it a bit stressful. Students from DTU got the exact same deadline, but weeks before I got the information.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is now awhile ago, but I don't remember it as very difficult.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was possible to write to Søren, who is the one from UCPH that is responsible for exchange students going to Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Getting the permission from UCPH was very slow, but applying at UQ was very easy. You can easily change courses at UQ, also in the beginning at the semester. It was my impression, that exchange students from other European countries had chosen more courses that they needed, so that they could try them out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that the courses were easier than studying at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: UQ has multiple assignments through out the semester, which could be between 5%-45% of your final grade. So I found that I had to pay more attention to deadlines through out the semester. Only one of the courses, I had, had a final exam whereas the others just had final assignments. The final assignments allows for greater flexibility.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Food for a Healthy Planet 
Cost Benefit Analysis & Project Evaluation
R and Python for the Life Sciences
Academic English & Thesis Writing for International Students

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: R and Python for the Life Sciences was the best course, I had. We were very few students in the classroom, and I had the experience that the content of the course was at the level, I expected. I gained a lot of useful knowledge by the completion of this course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay for Overseas Student Health Care (OSHC).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was very expensive. And I did use a lot of money for traveling, but that was my own choice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I joined so many clubs at the market day, which took place during O-week.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think there are more than 200 clubs, so I can't list all of them. I joined the mountain club, running club, skiing club, exchange club and the association for public health students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend QEUST, which is the exchange students club. It is a great way to meet other exchange students, and they offer trips to places near Brisbane. I also met some friends through this club, and we planned trips on our own. Besides that I'd recommend UQ SRC (the running club) and UQ MC (the mountain club). Both clubs are very social and a great opportunity to meet Australians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are so many places to go! Just nearby is the Gold Coast, Sunshine Coast, Glass House Mountains, Noosa, and Byron Bay. I'd definitely also recommend traveling further away to places like Melbourne, Sydney, and Tasmania.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found that Australia is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: You should join some of the clubs. In my experience socializing during classes is not that common.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found it a bit challenging that everything closes earlier than I'm used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very kind and easy to talk to. It's a very welcoming place to arrive.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) You should not stress about finding accommodation. It's very common that people make arrangements to see different flats before arriving without having anything in particular.
2) Be prepared to spend some money on traveling. Would be shame not to explore this great country. 
3) UQ has a lot thing happening through the semester (e.g. mental health week). Follow the student union on Instagram to see what's going on during the different weeks.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of right now.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many people, mostly from around Europe.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the high temperatures and the humidity. Also the sun sets very early.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
